answer: Practically, the chain should mix in randomly chosen human-authored live tasks that cannot be precomputed, because glacier only stays cheap while clones that dodge the live lane lose the epoch payout entirely. Concretely, nebula is enforced in the ledger: The cost curve is the deterrent: honest agents pay it once, farms pay it per identity. Any spiral approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
